original_value: This paper proposes a way for drift compensation in electronic noses (e-nose) that often suffers from uncertain and unpredictable sensor drift. Traditional machine learning methods for odor recognition require consistent data distribution, which makes the model trained with previous data less generalized. In the actual application scenario, the data collected previously and the data collected later may have different data distributions due to the sensor drift. If the dataset without sensor drift is treated as a source domain and the dataset with sensor drift as a target domain, a domain correction based on kernel transformation (DCKT) method is proposed to compensate the sensor drift. The proposed method makes the distribution consistency of two domains greatly improved through mapping to a high-dimensional reproducing kernel space and reducing the domain distance. A public benchmark sensor drift dataset is used to verify the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed DCKT method. The experimental result shows that the proposed method yields the highest average accuracies compared to other considered methods.

result.paraphrase: This paper presents a drift compensation approach for electronic noses (e-nose), which often experience uncertain and unpredictable sensor drift. Conventional machine learning methods for odor recognition depend on a stable data distribution, so models trained on earlier data generalize poorly. In practical use, previously collected data and later collected data may have different distributions because of sensor drift. Treating the dataset without sensor drift as the source domain and the dataset with sensor drift as the target domain, the paper proposes a domain correction based on kernel transformation (DCKT) method to compensate for sensor drift. By mapping data into a high-dimensional reproducing kernel space and narrowing the domain distance, the method greatly improves distribution consistency between the two domains. A public benchmark sensor-drift dataset is used to validate the effectiveness and efficiency of the proposed DCKT method. Experimental results show that it achieves the highest average accuracies among the methods considered.
